source: the structure of the ring sheet below and among the measured knots of ringfield.json: a ladder of octaves of ringlets by radius (plateaus with jittered edges; at each edge a groove and the slope of the step as a thin line), wave trains, and the hue each ringlet takes. Lengths in planet radii. Read by field.ts. The strengths per octave are set from the contrast by scale of the two approved images (assets-src/saturn/code/band_energy.py).
fromNote: the first octave that is worked out. In the hold the octaves from the widest down to 0.004 radii carry no strength: at those scales the sheet is the profile of the kept ring picture itself (ringfield.json), and the ladder adds only ringlets finer than that picture resolves; the two octaves before the first one with strength are still worked out there, because the bunches of an octave follow the octave two steps wider. Near the sheet the octaves from 0.032 radii on have strength (near.level, near.hue): the approved close image has wide soft lanes of grey beige, rose and blue grey in the foreground, and at the lens's height the kept profile has no structure of that width on screen. The first two octaves worked out have no wider octave to follow, so they stand at the low end of rough: in the dense rings they move the hue and hardly the brightness.
note: per octave, from the widest. level: how far a ringlet moves the logarithm of the brightness, in the dense rings and in the thin ones. slope: how bright the slope lines are when they face the Sun. tau is the share of the level that also moves the optical depth. rough and bunch: ringlets come in bunches, the strength of an octave runs between the two values of rough with a field that changes two octaves more slowly, over the two thresholds of bunch. edge is the half width of the edge of a ringlet in cells: the two widest octaves are soft zones of colour. filterFloor: the ladder is filtered with the pixel's footprint over the root of the samples of a frame, but never with less than this share of a pixel. even: from this octave on (too fine to see in the hold) the bunches are evener, the strength runs between these two values instead.
jitterNote: where in its cell a ringlet's edge lies: the first number plus the second times a value of its own (0 to 1), in cells

groove.note: the thin lines at the edges of the ringlets: half width in cells, narrowest and widest; the share of the range of strengths that gives no line; how far a dark line and a bright line move the logarithm of the brightness and how far a line moves the logarithm of the optical depth, per unit of strength; the strength per octave in the dense rings (strength) and in the thin ones (strengthThin), and the gain of each

hue.note: how far a ringlet moves the colour along two axes (warm to cool, rose to green), per octave from the widest, in the dense rings and in the thin ones; green: the share of the rose to green axis that is kept on its green side; gold: the share of the warm to cool axis that is kept on its warm side in the thin rings

waves.note: each train: radius of the resonance, length, wavelength at its far end, 1 for outward and -1 for inward. rise and fall are fractions of the length; tight caps how short the waves get near the resonance.

lanes.note: from this octave on the ringlets take turns, one bright and the next dark, by this amount (0: each ringlet has a level of its own): fine ringlets then carry little contrast at scales much wider than themselves, as in the approved close. A ringlet that takes its turn lies least + span * (its own value, 0 to 1) from the middle level, to the bright side or the dark side (the full range is 0.5 either way)

near.note: the strengths of the ladder for a camera near the sheet (the skim); the values above are for the hold. set.ts blends the two by the logarithm of the camera's height (skim.json light.heights). level, groove, hue, edge as above. groove.dark and groove.bright: the depth of a dark line and the gain of a bright one near the sheet (groove.dark and groove.bright above in the hold): in the approved close the ringlets of the thin rings are parted by grooves darker than the ice, so the dark lines are deeper near the sheet and they stand at the edges of the two widest octaves too (strengthThin), which keep their width under the shutter of the moving lens. rough and even: the two values of rough for the octaves below even.from and from it on, in the dense and in the thin rings. hue.follow: how far a brighter ringlet is also warmer and rosier (per unit of the logarithm of its brightness), in the dense and in the thin rings. footprints: an octave is drawn in full where its ringlets are twice this many footprints wide and not at all where they are this many (1 in the hold; a footprint is the pixel times filterFloor when a frame takes many samples, so 1.34 draws no ringlet under one pixel and every ringlet over two in full: finer ones only beat with the pixel grid). filter: as filter above, for the skim: the half width, in footprints, that the edges and the thin lines of the ringlets are widened to (1.2 gives a line nearly two pixels wide, which a steep line needs to read as one line and not as a rope).

wide.note: near the sheet a ringlet of the octave first on that is wide on screen (from so many footprints, in full from to) is drawn stronger: level is added to its level and its edge is edge cells soft instead of the octave's own. One that is wider still (hueFrom to hueTo footprints) keeps one minus hue of its hue (0: it keeps all of it), and its bright side is taken down: dark is how far the logarithm of the brightness of its brightest ringlet falls (its darkest keeps its level), so the broad ringlets near the lens read as grooves in the ice and not as white bands. The octaves before first are left as they are however wide they stand on screen: they are the wide soft lanes of the approved close image. So the picture has crisp ringlets at every width on screen down to the bottom edge, lying in soft lanes of colour. None of it in the hold.
